subject: computer-organization-and-architecture
subtopics: the memory hierarchy: levels from registers to disk, and the cost, speed and capacity trade at each level
locality of reference: temporal and spatial, and why the unit of transfer is a block rather than a word
memory characteristics: capacity, unit of transfer, access time against cycle time, volatility, and the SRAM-DRAM split
performance: hit time, miss penalty, hit ratio, and AMAT for a single level
AMAT for two levels of cache, with the miss rate of each level applied only to the accesses that reach it
the cache line, the set and the address split into tag, index and offset, with the width of each from the cache and block size
direct mapping: line = block mod lines, one comparator, and conflict misses
fully associative mapping: no index field, one comparator per line, and no conflict misses
set-associative mapping: sets and ways, set = block mod sets, and the index-to-tag shift when associativity changes
tag directory arithmetic: tag, valid, dirty and replacement bits per line, times the number of lines
replacement policies: LRU, FIFO, random and optimal, and an LRU trace over a reference string
write policies: write-through and write-back, write-allocate and no-write-allocate, and what the dirty bit implies
block size and the three kinds of miss: compulsory, conflict and capacity
memory interfacing: chip count in two dimensions, address decoding, chip select and a chip's address range
memory interleaving: high-order and low-order, which address bits name the bank, and the bandwidth it buys

chosen.title: Lecture 24 - Basics of Memory and Cache (Memory System, unit 1 part 1)
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Computer Organization and Architecture - A Pedagogical Aspect (Prof. J. K. Deka, Dr. Santosh Biswas, Dr. Arnab Sarkar, IIT Guwahati)
covers: memory split into inboard (registers, cache, main memory), outboard (disks, optical) and offline bulk storage
capacity defined as the number of distinctly addressable locations times the size of a location
unit of transfer as the number of bits moved at one time, determined by the data bus, with word size equal to it in this course
byte addressing against word addressing, and the statement that the higher-order bits of a 32-bit address name a word while the low two name a byte inside it
chosen.why: The only readable source this run that defines capacity and unit of transfer as measurements rather than as slogans, which is what the memory-characteristics card needs. Read in part: the served extract runs from the unit's objectives through memory addressing and stops before the direct-mapped cache design it promises, so nothing is attributed to that later section.

chosen.title: Lecture 25 - Direct-mapped Caches: Misses, Writes and Performance
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Computer Organization and Architecture - A Pedagogical Aspect (IIT Guwahati)
covers: the memory-technology comparison in access time and cost per GB: SRAM about 0.5 to 2.5 ns and 2000 to 5000 dollars per GB, DRAM 50 to 70 ns and 20 to 75 dollars per GB, disks 5 to 20 ms and 0.2 to 2 dollars per GB
the design trade-off that forces a hierarchy, and the statement that as one goes down it cost per GB falls, capacity rises and access time rises
locality of reference with temporal locality (loop instructions) and spatial locality (sequential array access) as two distinct principles
hit time, hit ratio and miss defined on a read, with the cache described as SRAM between the CPU and main memory
chosen.why: The clearest statement read this run of why a hierarchy exists at all, with the numbers that make it concrete, and of hit time and hit ratio as definitions rather than formulas. Read in part: the extract ends inside the locality discussion, so the lecture's treatment of write policy and its own performance examples are not used.

chosen.title: Lecture 26 - Associative and Multi-Level Caches (line size, miss penalty, early restart)
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Computer Organization and Architecture - A Pedagogical Aspect (IIT Guwahati)
covers: why a larger line lowers the miss rate through spatial locality, and why the miss rate rises again once the line becomes a significant fraction of the cache because the number of lines falls
miss penalty defined as the time to fetch a line from the next lower level of the hierarchy and load it into the cache
miss penalty split into the latency of the first word and the transfer time for the rest of the block, and why a larger line therefore costs more per miss
early restart as resuming execution when the requested word arrives instead of waiting for the whole block, and why it works best for instruction fetches
chosen.why: The only readable source that states the block-size trade-off as a mechanism on both sides - spatial locality gained, lines and transfer time lost - and that defines miss penalty as a sum of two parts, which the AMAT card depends on. Read in part: the served text stops inside the early-restart discussion, so the lecture's own multi-level treatment is not attributed to it.

chosen.title: Computer Organization: Memory Hierarchy and Cache Memories
chosen.channel: Indian Institute of Science, Centre for Data Sciences, computer architecture and organization slides
covers: main memory as about 100 times slower than the CPU, with the cache as the solution and locality of reference as the design principle
a cache decomposed into sets of lines, each line holding a valid bit, a tag and a data block of B bytes
the address divided into tag, index and offset, with the index selecting the set, the tags compared inside it, the offset picking the word, and a hit requiring valid and a tag match
direct-mapped caches as one line per set with conflict misses as their disadvantage, m-way associativity as m lines per set, and fully associative as one set holding all lines
a worked 16 KB direct-mapped cache with 32 B blocks given as tag 18, index 9, offset 5
chosen.why: The source of the line-as-valid-bit-tag-and-block description and of the lookup sequence, and the only readable source that gives a complete three-field split for a named configuration. Read in part: the extraction returned the locality, address-composition, lookup and mapping sections plus the worked 16 KB example; the later cache-and-programming examples were read only as far as the vector-sum miss counts.

chosen.title: Memory System Design (ELEX 2117, Digital Techniques 2)
chosen.channel: University of British Columbia, Electrical and Computer Engineering, lecture 9 notes
covers: the memory-interface signals and what each one does: address, data, CS to enable a read or write, OE to turn the data bus into an output, WE to write
tri-state outputs as the reason only one device may drive the shared data bus at a time
memory ICs combined in parallel to widen the word, all of them sharing the control signals, with the number of ICs in a bank being word size divided by IC word size
banks of those rows extending the address range, the number of banks being total words divided by words per IC, each bank needing its own chip select
address decoding as the circuit that decides where a bank sits in the memory map, with memories placed at multiples of their size to simplify it
chosen.why: The only readable source that states the two dimensions of chip count as rules and ties them to chip select and decoding, which is the whole of the interfacing card. Read in part: the extraction returned the terminology, interface signals and timing sections in full and the memory-array and decoding rules; the host refused both a direct request and a plain fetch from this sandbox, so the text came through the extraction service.

chosen.title: Lecture 13 - Memory Interface (EE2 Digital Electronics)
chosen.channel: Imperial College London, Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Dr Peter Cheung
covers: the inside of a RAM chip: a row decoder producing one-hot row selects, a column multiplexer driven by the less significant address bits, and CE, OE and WE with the tri-state data bus
an address space partitioned into 32 KB of RAM, 16 KB of ROM and 4 KB of input/output, with only A15:12 decoded into enable signals and A11:0 used inside the parts
the statement that selecting which memory sub-system, and therefore which chip, to enable is the job of the address decoder, and that without a decoder only one device could be attached
a worked ROM enable condition over a range of the top four address bits
chosen.why: The only readable source that shows a decoder choosing between several parts of unequal size and states the split between the bits that select a part and the bits used inside it, which is what the chip-select card teaches. Read in part: the extraction returned the chip-internals and address-decoding sections and stopped inside the timing discussion; the host refuses direct requests from this sandbox.

chosen.title: Cache Memory & Mapping Hindi mein
chosen.channel: DSWallah Learn (Hinglish study lesson on cache memory)
covers: locality of reference as the assumption that makes a cache possible at all, with temporal and spatial locality named and the block rather than the word as the unit of transfer
the three mapping techniques with their formulas: line = block mod total lines, set = block mod total sets, and full associativity with no index field
AMAT as hit time plus miss rate times miss penalty, and the two-level form that adds the L2 time on an L1 miss
write-through, write-back, write-allocate and no-write-allocate defined, with the dirty bit as the record of a modified block
its list of common mistakes, including saying line = block divided by total lines instead of modulo, and dropping the hit time from AMAT
chosen.why: The only non-English source readable this run, and the only one that states AMAT and the two-level form together with the write-policy vocabulary as a single consistent set. Written in romanised Hindi and translated into English here, and marked as translated on the six cards it feeds. Its parking analogy, its exercise questions and its advice about which topics other examinations ask are not used; its claim that write-back is the default in most modern CPUs is not repeated, because no source read this run supports it.

chosen.title: Memory Interleaving
covers: interleaving as distributing addresses across modules round-robin so that a module is busy while another is accessed
the high-order arrangement, in which the most significant bits name the module and a module holds a consecutive run of addresses
the low-order arrangement, in which the least significant bits name the module so that consecutive words sit in different modules
the benefit stated as bandwidth from parallel banks rather than as a shorter single access
chosen.why: Read in full, and the only readable source that sets the two arrangements side by side with the bit that names the module in each. It is a revision digest and derives nothing, so the timing arithmetic on the interleaving card is this repository's own and is recomputed rather than quoted.

rejected.channel: R. Pacalet, Telecom Paris / EURECOM, Computer Architecture - Caches
rejected.why: The most complete cache deck found - direct-mapped, set-associative, replacement, write policies, write buffers, coherence, and a worked 32-bit example - and it could not be read: the host returned 502 to a direct request and to the extraction service, and only search extracts were readable. William Stallings, Computer Organization and Architecture - cache memory organisation, replacement algorithms, write policies and multilevel caches

GATE 2027 CS syllabus, Computer Organization and Architecture line 'Memory interfacing and hierarchy: performance, cache memory mapping'
Official GATE CSE papers and answer keys for the twelve recorded questions - not fetched this run, which is why every PYQ here is SOURCED rather than key-verified
notes: The syllabus names this topic in one line, 'Memory interfacing and hierarchy: performance, cache memory mapping', so the fifteen subtopics above are this run's enumeration from the standard treatment (Patterson-Hennessy, Hamacher chapter 8, Mano chapter 12, Stallings), from the IIT Guwahati memory module's own five-lecture structure and from the GATE question record - not a quotation from the syllabus. Every one of the fifteen has a card, which is why the status is partial rather than lower; the gaps below are what keep it from being covered.

Twelve GATE CSE previous-year questions were verified, from 2009 to 2025, and every one is SOURCED against an accepted answer rather than key-verified, so no marks field comes from an official key. Two of them (2024 Set 1 Q.43 and 2017 Set 1 Q.54) are additionally reported by a third-party page as carrying the same official answer, and that is recorded in their answer_evidence rather than used to upgrade the label.

No video transcript was readable this run. Every YouTube watch page tried served a description and no usable caption track, so videoRefs is empty on all fifteen cards and no card quotes or timestamps a lecture. The teaching rests on four NPTEL lecture transcripts published as PDFs, three university lecture decks and two written lessons.

One non-English source was readable, a romanised-Hindi written lesson, and it is marked translated on the six cards it feeds. It supplies the AMAT formulation, the two-level form, the write-policy vocabulary and the three mapping formulas in one consistent set. No Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or Bengali lecture transcript could be read.

Two of the eight chosen sources were reachable only through the extraction service, because their hosts refused direct requests from this sandbox; three others (the Telecom Paris cache deck, the IIT Delhi memory lectures and Hamacher chapter 8) returned 502 or 403 on every route and are recorded as rejected or as standard references only.

Every numeric claim published in this topic is recomputed in scripts/validate.py: the tag, index and offset widths of six configurations, the directory sizes, the twelve PYQ answers including two full cache simulations and two chip-select decodes, the AMAT arithmetic, the interleaving timing, and every number shown in the two visual lessons.

The interleaving timing arithmetic (bank cycle plus bus cycle times the remaining words, and the condition under which the overlap holds) is this repository's own. The readable interleaving source states the two arrangements and the bandwidth benefit and derives no timing, so the formula is recomputed rather than quoted, and the card says so in its source line.

GATE CSE 2020 Q.21 is recorded with the answer 13.5 and with the recorded dissent that the official key also accepted 13.3, because the source textbook example adds the cache delay explicitly and the question does not.
The 2017 Set 1 tag question is recorded as Q.54 on GATE Overflow with the three other numbering conventions named, because four sites disagree about its number.
